senses.gloss: youth; inferior position. Lam. R. introd. (R. Joh. 1) אוי … שבקַטְנוּתוֹ וכ׳ woe to the king who succeeded when he was young but failed in his old age.
units: <cite ref="Megillah 11a:18">Meg. 11ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>הקטן</he>, <cite ref="I Samuel 17:14">I Sam. XVII, 14</cite>) <he>כשם שבקטנותו הקטין וכ׳</he> as in his inferior position he (David) subordinated himself to one greater …, so when he was king &c.; a. e.

senses.gloss: humility, modesty. Ib. הוא בקטנותו he was always the same as to his humility.

units: <cite ref="Sotah 48b:20">Sot. 48ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Zechariah 4:10">Zech. IV, 10</cite>) <he>מי גרם … ק׳ שהיתה בהן שלא האמינו וכ׳</he> (not <cite ref="U00304"><he>שהיה</he></cite>) what causes the table of the righteous in the hereafter to be contemptible? The pusillanimity that was in them, in that they had no faith in God; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 571:2">Yalk. Zech. 571</cite>.

Sot. IX, 15 (49ᵃ) Abba José was surnamed קטונתא, שהיה קַטְנוּתָן של וכ׳ (Y. ed. תמצותן; Bab. ed. קטנתא) because he was the tail-end (the last) of the pious men (v. קָטֹן, Nithpa.); (ib. 49ᵇ שהיה מקטני חסידים, v. preced. w.).
